title: TRAILER B — "Every Sport Has a Sound" (Unit 4 entire)
_thesis: Not the historical spine. Unit 4 alone, at close range: the modern athletes' OWN equipment, worn and swung and struck, each object making its own noise. Percussive, fast, contemporary, cut on impact. Where Trailer A is ceremonial and chronological, this one is bodily and simultaneous — it does not tell a history, it makes a rhythm.
_hard_rule: NO ARTEFACT APPEARS ALONE. Every shot declares its artefact in `carries` AND shows a body using it. Philipp's two named examples are shots b3 (the shoes on the athlete at the long-jump board) and b4 (two fencers engaged, mask worn and épée in hand).
_text_rule: Several of these objects carry signatures, squad numbers or handwritten inscriptions. The 2026-08-04 route-list failure established that lists and handwriting do NOT survive generation — every letterform can be perfect while the content is duplicated or invented. NO SHOT HERE RESTS ON LEGIBLE TEXT. Every inscription is either out of frame, in motion, or under water.
style: Contemporary sports cinematography, cool desaturated blue-grey with a warm skin note, crushed blacks, hard single-source key, shallow focus, fine grain, sweat and dust and spray visible in the light. Photographic realism, natural skin texture, no stylisation, no legible signage, no brand marks, no text or captions anywhere in frame. NO Olympic rings, NO national flags, NO federation emblems, NO sponsor boards, NO banners with lettering anywhere in frame including far background and out of focus: generated emblems come out malformed and the rings are a restricted mark, so a blurred approximation is a liability rather than set dressing.

shots.title: U4 · THE BOARD — the shoes hit at 8.41
shots.image_type: Cinematic film still, photoreal, shot on a real location. No captions, no signage, no scoreboard, no bib number.
shots._text_conflict_resolved: SM_RV_18's registry invariant requires the athlete's handwritten ink ('8.41', the Greek name, 'TOKIO 2020') because on a STILL of the object that handwriting IS the hero detail. This shot is the opposite case: the shoe is on a moving foot at the instant of takeoff. Carrying the blanket 'no text anywhere in frame' rule here put two contradictory instructions in one prompt and the model returned no image at all. Resolved by scoping: the ink is PRESENT on the object and simply not resolvable at this scale and speed — which is true of a real photograph too — while captions, signage and bib numbers stay banned.
shots.subject_action: A long jumper at the instant of takeoff, WEARING the white competition shoes. The athlete's own handwritten ink is on the shoe but is NOT legible at this scale and speed — present, not readable; do not sharpen it and do not invent it. The planting foot is FLAT ON THE TAKEOFF BOARD with the shoe compressed under the load, the other leg already driving through. Ahead of him is the sand.
shots.shot_type: Low side-on shot, the athlete from the waist down, the takeoff board running across the lower frame.
shots.camera_angle: Low, near runway level, square to the runway so the board reads as a clean horizontal.
shots.lens: 85mm, f/2.0 — the planted shoe and the board edge sharp, the runway behind and the sand ahead falling off.
shots.spatial_composition: The planted shoe and the board sit at LOWER CENTRE-LEFT. A CLEAR OPEN CORRIDOR of sand pit runs away to the RIGHT with nothing in it — the space he is about to travel through. No official, no marker, no other athlete anywhere in frame. No board markings, no scoreboard, no bib number.

A CLEAR RUN of empty piste extends beyond each fencer. NO third figure, no official, no scoreboard, nothing crossing the blade line.

shots._why_not_artefact: The Sydney 2000 ensemble is digitised as THREE separate apparatus — SM_RV_8 club, SM_RV_11 ball, SM_RV_7 hoop. The word 'gymnastics' matches all three. The object that falls in this shot is the CLUB, SM_RV_8, and it is carried. The ball and hoop are not in frame and must not be threaded in: it was the club that was dropped. SM_RV_7 (Karyami hoop) added 2026-08-28: the word 'gymnastics' matches it since the registry grew to 23; the hoop is genuinely not in this shot.
